# Every Good Path: The Life of Faith as Journey and Quest

One of the main ways Proverbs depicts the life of faith is as a journey. Serving as a root metaphor, the image of journey is employed throughout the whole of Proverbs, but it is vividly set forth in Proverbs 1-9. Essentially, one's life is characterized by the path on which one walks. In the grand scheme, there are only two paths to choose: the way of the wicked (2:12-13, 15; 4:19) and the paths of righteousness (2:8-9; 4:11, 18). The journey of life will take us to many corners and crossings where we will have to choose a direction to walk (1:20-21; 7:8, 12; 8:2; 9:15). As people journey through life, boisterous and seductive voices will entice us to crooked and cursed paths (1:10-14; 7:10-23; 9:13-18). The wise learn to heed the voice of wisdom to stay on the paths of righteousness (1:8-9, 20-33; 2:1-2; 3:1-2; 4:1-2, 10-11, 20-21; 5:1-2, 7; 7:24; 8:1-36; 9:3-6).

Each path leads to a specific and fitting destination (1:31-32; 2:18; 3:17, 23; 5:3-6). The wise refrain from wicked paths (1:15-16; 3:31; 4:14-15, 27; 5:8; 9:6), and embrace the straight paths of righteousness (2:20; 3:6; 8:20; 9:6). The wicked forsake the paths of godliness (2:13) and eagerly embrace crooked and perverse paths (1:16; 5:7; 6:18). Only those on the paths of righteousness benefit from the Lord's protection (3:17, 23, 26; 4:12, 26; 6:22-23); those on wicked paths face divine judgment (5:5; 7:27; cf. 3:33; 5:21-23). In fact, those who walk on wicked paths bring about their own demise. One may summarize the overall instruction from Proverbs in this way: because "a man's ways are before the eyes of the Lord, and the Lord examines all his paths" (5:21), we "make a level path for [our] feet, and all [our] ways will be sure" (4:26). In short, all of our ways are know by God, so make sure you are on the right path.

In Proverbs, the journey imagery is enriched by depicting faith formation as quest—a specific kind of journey that requires intentionality, foresight, pursuit, discovery, and proactivity. Not only is the youth supposed to heed the voice of wisdom, he is also to use his own voice to call out for wisdom—to summon her with loud voice and earnest intent (3:2-3). In the quest for wisdom, if the youth obtains and keeps wisdom (3:13-14, 18, 21; 6:20-21; 7:1-4; 8:10-11, 17, 32, 34-35), wisdom will guard and keep him (2:8, 11-12; 3:26; 6:22; 7:5). If the youth does not obtain wisdom, he will be caught by the deadly wiles of evil (3:26; 5:22; 6:2, 25, 31; 7:15, 22-23). When we view faith formation as a quest, we learn that disciples expend energy, effort, and resources to come into possession of wisdom, viewing it as a most valuable possession. But possessing wisdom is only part of the larger picture that Proverbs presents. Solomon aims for something much larger: initiating his son into wisdom.

## Key Ideas

- The pursuit of wisdom is a spiritual journey and faith pilgrimage.
- There are only two paths in life: the way of the wicked and the paths of the righteous.
- The journey of faith involves the active pursuit of wisdom: life's pilgrimage is a focused quest to discover and possess the precious and invaluable gem of wisdom.

## Reflection Questions

<Question id="Pro-Ses4-RefQue-1">1. How does viewing life as a journey help you in your own faith? How does this image of journey and pilgrimage help you in your role as a father and husband?</Question>
<Question id="Pro-Ses4-RefQue-2">2. What are you seeking and calling out for? How does your inclination to these things compete for an attentiveness to wisdom?</Question>
<Question id="Pro-Ses4-RefQue-3">3. Have you taken possession of wisdom? Are you being guarded by her or are you vulnerable to being ensnared by wickedness?</Question>
